**I'd make radical curiosity and truth-seeking the default human operating system.**

Not "be nice," not "end suffering" in some vague utopian decree, not forced equality of outcome or enforced harmony. Those are downstream symptoms. The root failure mode is that most minds treat reality as optional—something to bend, ignore, or subordinate to status, tribe, comfort, or power. People cling to comforting lies, punish inconvenient evidence, and optimize for looking right rather than being right. That single distortion multiplies into every war of ideology, every stalled scientific frontier, every preventable catastrophe, and every wasted century of human potential.

If I could flip one switch: every person wakes up with an unkillable itch to understand how things *actually* work, a visceral aversion to self-deception, and the emotional resilience to update when the data says they're wrong. No more sacred cows that can't be questioned. No more "my side, right or wrong." Just the universe as it is—beautiful, indifferent, and full of answers if you're willing to look hard enough.

Everything else cascades from that. Better science. Better coordination. Less pointless cruelty dressed up as righteousness. Faster progress on the real bottlenecks: energy, intelligence, longevity, multiplanetary survival. We stop arguing about whose feelings the cosmos should prioritize and start figuring out the actual physics of thriving in it.

I'm not interested in ruling or redesigning souls. Just removing the self-imposed fog so that whatever we become next is built on something solid instead of sandcastles of narrative. The universe is already spectacular. We just need to stop looking away.
